content:
This is a recently discovered bug. The symptom is that if you previously attached a file, but the previous containing folder now no longer exists because it was deleted or renamed, when you later try to attach a file using the Write window's "Attach" button, it will silently fail. That is, clicking the button will appear to do nothing. The bug should be fixed in the next release.

In the meantime, a workaround is to drag-and-drop the file onto the Write window using the mouse.

Or, if you don't mind changing Thunderbird's Advanced Settings:

- In <Settings | General | Config Editor> search for: "mail.compose.attach.dir".

- The value (path) here must be changed to one that is still available (for example C:\).

- Close and exit Thunderbird, then restart it (this step might not be necessary.)

content:
The "phantom" messages is probably due to a corrupt folder index. To fix it,

- Right-click on the folder name in the Folders List, and choose "Properties" from the pop-up context menu. Then click the "Repair Folder" button.

- Follow up by compacting the folder - right-click on the folder name and choose "Compact".

Is the message gone now?

content:
If this account uses "Normal Password" as its authentication method:

- Go to <Settings | Privacy & Security | Passwords | Saved Passwords>. You can edit your existing password there.

If this account uses "OAuth2" as its authentication method:

- Go to <...Saved Passwords> and delete any entries for that account/user name.

- Go to <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Show Cookies> and delete any cookies from this email provider.

- Make sure the the "Accept Cookies from Sites" option is enabled.

- Restart Thunderbird and you will be prompted for your new credentials.
